settings.appearance.bad_color: The saved color “{color}” is not in the #rrggbb format: pages stay violet for now
settings.appearance.help: The accent color and the report language are the same for the whole installation and all areas. The accent marks the logo, the tab icon, the focus ring and the SLA zone of charts; buttons and tabs stay neutral. The interface theme and language are chosen separately, in the View menu of the top bar.
settings.appearance.language_hint: Applies to new reports, forecast explanations and document import. Ready reports do not change. Everyone chooses the interface language in the View menu of the top bar.
settings.area.global_note: Pick an area in the top bar to set overrides for it; without an area you edit the defaults for all areas.
settings.area.global_note_initial: Pick an area in the top bar to set overrides for it; without an area you edit the defaults.
settings.area.pick: Pick an area in the top bar
settings.area.required: {action}: pick an area in the top bar first
settings.area.scoped_note: The data source catalog is shared. Domain bindings, LLM, SLA, queries, prompts and visualizations are saved as overrides of this area. Storage and Confluence are shared.
settings.area.unknown_note: The settings have no area “{area}”: pick an area in the top bar.
settings.binding.bucket.label: Flux bucket
settings.binding.database.label: InfluxQL database
settings.binding.datasource_name.label: Data source name
settings.binding.datasource_uid.label: Data source UID
settings.binding.datasource_uid.placehol: if the name is not unique
settings.binding.default_row_note: for domains without their own row
settings.binding.ds_list_failed: Grafana returned no data source list
settings.binding.ds_none: Grafana has no Prometheus or InfluxDB data sources
settings.binding.ds_unavailable: The data source list is unavailable: {error}
settings.binding.need_catalog: First add and save a source in the “Data sources” card.
settings.binding.prometheus_direct: No extra parameters: queries go straight to Prometheus
settings.binding.source_not_saved: The source is not in the saved catalog: save the catalog or pick another one
settings.card.confluence.desc: Publishes a finished report as a Confluence page with a button on the report page (analysis tabs and charts).
settings.card.confluence.title: Confluence: web report publishing
settings.card.confluence_template.desc: The classic report on creation: a copy of the template page, Grafana panel snapshots and a Loki log export. The template IDs are set in the “Visualizations” section.
settings.card.confluence_template.title: Confluence template, Grafana render, Loki
settings.card.data_sources.desc: Connections to Grafana, Prometheus and InfluxDB: address and account. One connection can serve several domains.
settings.card.data_sources.title: Data sources
settings.card.default_params.desc: The query step for metric sources and the time series aggregation interval before analysis.
settings.card.default_params.title: Sampling parameters
settings.card.domain_sources.desc: Where each domain takes its metrics from. For Grafana pick a data source; the list comes from Grafana itself. An area's own binding replaces the global one as a whole.
settings.card.domain_sources.title: Domain sources
settings.card.llm.desc: The model that writes the domain and final reports. The check sends a short request and spends a few tokens.
settings.card.llm.title: LLM provider (AI analysis)
settings.card.load_generators.desc: Servers where the “Run test” page starts load testing tools over SSH, and a manual mode where LoadLens only marks the start and end of a run. Engineers can run tests: give LoadLens its own user on the generator.
settings.card.load_generators.title: Load generators
settings.card.load_tools.desc: Command templates of k6, JMeter, Locust and Gatling for the “Run test” page. Only differences from the built-in templates are saved.
settings.card.load_tools.title: Load testing tools
settings.card.logs_source.desc: Optional domain: aggregated ERROR logs of the test window go into the AI analysis.
settings.card.logs_source.title: Application logs (OpenSearch)
settings.card.storage.desc: The database that holds metrics, reports and job states. Every page needs it.
settings.card.storage.title: Storage (TimescaleDB)
settings.connections.help: Fill in the key fields and click “Test connection”: the check uses the form data before anything is saved. Rarely used parameters are in the “Advanced parameters (JSON)” block. Passwords and tokens are shown as {mask} and are stored on the server only. The source catalog is shared by all areas; domain bindings and the LLM can be overridden for the selected area. Storage and Confluence are shared.
settings.context.heading: Context of the system under test
settings.context.help: A description of the system, its components, critical flows and risks. The AI analysis uses it as background, and a snapshot is saved with every report. Fill in what you know: empty blocks do no harm. A service can have its own context, which replaces the area context as a whole.
settings.ctx.components.name: Name
settings.ctx.components.title: Components
settings.ctx.critical_user_flows.name: Flow
settings.ctx.critical_user_flows.title: Critical flows
settings.ctx.data_stores.title: Data stores
settings.ctx.dependencies.title: Dependencies
settings.ctx.enabled: Pass the context to the AI analysis
settings.ctx.entrypoints.name: Name
settings.ctx.entrypoints.title: Entry points
settings.ctx.group.architecture_hint: Components and dependencies help the AI link metrics of different domains.
settings.ctx.group.load_model_hint: Shows the AI which entry points and flows matter most to the business.
settings.ctx.group.operational_context_h: Goes into the prompt as the customer's rules: what counts as normal and what to focus on.
settings.ctx.group.system_hint: Sent to the AI with the metrics of every domain.
settings.ctx.import.file_hint: PDF with a text layer, Word (.docx), Markdown or plain text, up to 10 MB. Scans without text cannot be read.
settings.ctx.import.file_too_big: The file is larger than 10 MB
settings.ctx.import.filled: The context is filled in from {from}. Check the highlighted fields and save.
settings.ctx.import.mode_fill: Merge: fill in empty fields and add new items
settings.ctx.import.mode_replace: Replace: the whole context from the document
settings.ctx.import.need_text: Paste a description of the system: at least a few sentences
settings.ctx.import.need_url: Paste the full link to the Confluence page
settings.ctx.import.no_llm: No LLM provider is set up: set it first in the “LLM” card of the “Connections” section.
settings.ctx.import.no_response: The server does not answer, try again
settings.ctx.import.nothing: Parsing {from} gave nothing new for this context.
settings.ctx.import.parsing: The model is parsing the document… usually 20–60 s
settings.ctx.import.parsing_elapsed: The model is parsing the document… {n} s passed
settings.ctx.import.text_placeholder: Paste a description of the system: purpose, components, dependencies, flows, risks…
settings.ctx.import.title: Fill in the context from a document
settings.ctx.import.url_hint: A page from {base} is read with the account of the Confluence connection. The page address from the browser or a short link will do.
settings.ctx.import.url_hint_unset: First set up the Confluence connection in the “Connections” section: the page is read with its account.
settings.ctx.import.warning: The text of the document or page is sent to the model {model} from the LLM settings. Nothing is saved until you click “Save” in the form.
settings.ctx.line.known_risks: Known risks — check against the data
settings.ctx.note.service_inherits: The service uses the area context
settings.ctx.system.name: Name
settings.field.confluence.enabled.label: Allow publishing
settings.field.confluence.forecast_paren: Capacity forecast reports are created as its child pages; empty means the same page as for reports
settings.field.confluence.parent_page_id: Reports are created as its child pages
settings.field.confluence.password.label: Password
settings.field.confluence.username.label: Login
settings.field.default_params.step.label: Sampling step
settings.field.gen.docker_ca_cert.label: CA certificate
settings.field.gen.docker_cpus.label: CPU per container
settings.field.gen.docker_url.label: Docker API address
settings.field.gen.env.hint: For every tool on this generator, one NAME=value per line.
settings.field.gen.env.label: Generator environment variables
settings.field.gen.gitlab_api_token.hint: Reads parameters and status, starts and cancels the pipeline. With read_api LoadLens only reads.
settings.field.gen.gitlab_inputs.label: Inputs (spec:inputs) through the API
settings.field.gen.gitlab_project.label: Project
settings.field.gen.gitlab_ref.label: Default branch
settings.field.gen.gitlab_ref.placeholde: empty means the project's default branch
Trigger token (if there is no API token)
settings.field.gen.gitlab_url.label: GitLab address
settings.field.gen.jenkins_job.label: Job
settings.field.gen.jenkins_ref.label: Default branch of a multibranch job
settings.field.gen.jenkins_ref.placehold: empty means main or the first one
settings.field.gen.jenkins_url.label: Jenkins address
settings.field.gen.k8s_api_url.label: Kubernetes API address
settings.field.gen.k8s_ca_cert.label: Cluster CA certificate
settings.field.gen.k8s_config_map.label: ConfigMap with scripts
settings.field.gen.k8s_cpu.label: Pod CPU
settings.field.gen.k8s_in_cluster.label: LoadLens runs in this cluster (the pod's service account)
settings.field.gen.k8s_memory.label: Pod memory
settings.field.gen.k8s_namespace.label: Namespace
settings.field.gen.k8s_pvc.label: Or a PVC with scripts
settings.field.gen.k8s_token.label: Service account token
settings.field.gen.k8s_ttl_seconds.label: Keep a finished Job, s
settings.field.gen.loadlens_url.hint: Optional. The pipeline can send started and finished to it with the LOADLENS_EVENTS_URL and LOADLENS_TOKEN variables; without events the window comes from CI and is narrowed by RPS.
settings.field.gen.loadlens_url.label: LoadLens address for pipeline events
settings.field.gen.max_parallel.label: Instances at a time
settings.field.gen.mounts.hint: One per line: a volume or an absolute path on the Docker host, the path in the container, and ro or rw.
settings.field.gen.mounts.label: Mounts
settings.field.gen.network.label: Container network
settings.field.gen.param_options.hint: For parameters whose options CI does not return (Active Choices with a script): NAME=option1, option2. The field becomes a choice in the run form.
settings.field.gen.param_options.label: Parameter options
settings.field.gen.remove_finished.label: Remove the container when it finishes (the log stays in the run)
settings.field.gen.scripts_dir.hint: Relative paths start here; the run form looks for scripts here.
settings.field.gen.scripts_dir.label: Scripts directory
settings.field.gen.ssh_host.label: Address
settings.field.gen.ssh_host_key.hint: The check shows the fingerprint of the server key; once you confirm it the key is pinned, then save the generator. Without a host key LoadLens will not connect to run tests.
settings.field.gen.ssh_host_key.label: Host key
settings.field.gen.ssh_passphrase.label: Key passphrase
settings.field.gen.ssh_password.label: Password (instead of a key)
settings.field.gen.ssh_port.label: SSH port
settings.field.gen.ssh_private_key.hint: ed25519, ECDSA or RSA in OpenSSH or PEM format. Create a separate user for LoadLens on the generator.
settings.field.gen.ssh_private_key.label: Private key
settings.field.gen.ssh_username.label: User
settings.field.gen.tags_metrics.hint: Then live charts and the report tell the run's metrics from other tests by the tag; otherwise only by the time window.
settings.field.gen.tags_metrics.label: The pipeline passes LOADLENS_RUN_TAG to the tool (metrics carry the run tag)
settings.field.gen.title.label: Name
settings.field.gen.verify.label: Verify the TLS certificate
settings.field.gen.work_dir.hint: Instance directories: log, exit code and service files.
settings.field.gen.work_dir.label: Working directory
settings.field.llm.api_key.label: API key
settings.field.llm.context_window_tokens: Input and answer together must fit the model window.
settings.field.llm.gigachat_verify.label: Verify the API TLS certificate
settings.field.llm.max_concurrent.label: Parallel requests
settings.field.llm.max_domain_workers.hi: How many domains to analyze at the same time
settings.field.llm.max_tokens.hint: Reserved for the answer: the input is cut to fit the rest of the window.
settings.field.llm.max_tokens.label: Max response tokens
settings.field.llm.model.label: Model
settings.field.llm.provider.label: Provider
settings.field.llm.self_consistency_k.hi: Number of answer variants the judge picks the best one from
settings.field.logs_source.enabled.label: Enable the “Application logs” domain
settings.field.source.influxdb_org.label: Organization
settings.field.source.title.label: Name
settings.field.storage.dbname.label: Database
settings.field.storage.host.label: Host
settings.field.storage.password.label: Password
settings.field.storage.port.label: Port
settings.field.storage.schema.label: Schema
settings.field.storage.user.label: User
settings.field.tool.command.hint: Substitutions: {exe} {exe_dir} {script} {script_dir} {scripts_dir} {run_name} {run_tag} {instance} {instance_tag} {instance_dir} {control_port}. {params} is the parameters from the run form, as a separate word.
settings.field.tool.command.label: Command
settings.field.tool.cwd.label: Working directory
settings.field.tool.env.hint: A value with the same name from the run form is appended after a space (handy for JAVA_OPTS).
settings.field.tool.env.label: Environment variables
settings.field.tool.executable.hint: Replaces {exe}; a generator can set its own path.
settings.field.tool.executable.label: Executable
settings.field.tool.grace_seconds.label: Wait after the signal, s
settings.field.tool.help.label: Hint in the run form
settings.field.tool.image.label: Image for Docker and Kubernetes
settings.field.tool.run_filter_packs.hin: Only if the command really tags the metrics with {run_tag}. Otherwise the run's metrics are told apart by the window.
settings.field.tool.run_filter_packs.lab: Query packs that see the run tag
settings.field.tool.script_kind.label: What is picked as the script
settings.field.tool.scripts_glob.label: Script masks
settings.field.tool.status_command.hint: Every 15 s; the answer is shown at the instance (k6: number of VUs).
settings.field.tool.status_command.label: Status command
settings.field.tool.stop_command.hint: Runs next to the tool instead of a signal (SSH and Docker); on an error the signal is sent. {control_port} is the instance control port.
settings.field.tool.stop_command.label: Graceful stop command
settings.field.tool.stop_signal.label: Stop signal
settings.field.tool.title.label: Name
settings.form.id_rule: ID: lowercase Latin letters, digits, hyphen and underscore, up to 40 characters
settings.form.title: Name
settings.gen.check_recorded: The check result is written to the generator: save the section
settings.gen.empty: No generators yet. Add a server with load testing tools installed, or a manual generator.
settings.gen.host_key_message: The server {where} presented the host key {key}. Compare the fingerprint with the key on the server itself, for example with ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub. Once you confirm it, LoadLens connects only to a server with this key.
settings.gen.summary.manual: LoadLens only marks the start and end of a run
settings.gen.tools.all: No list is set: the run form offers every tool. {note}
settings.gen.tools.label: Tools on the generator
settings.gen.tools.note_ci: The CI job runs the tool in its own image: set only the executable name here, if it differs.
settings.gen.tools.note_container: The image tells where to find the tool; an empty image is taken from the tool template. Tools without an image do not appear in the run form.
settings.gen.tools.note_ssh: Enter your own path if the tool is not installed where the template looks.
settings.gen.tools.some: The run form offers only the ticked tools. {note}
settings.gen.type.docker_hint: A container per instance through the Docker Engine API: https://host:2376 with client certificates, or a socket proxy. Access to the Docker API equals root on the host.
settings.gen.type.gitlab_hint: Runs your pipeline as is: the pipeline sets the tool, the script and their settings, while LoadLens picks the branch and the values of its parameters (variables with a description and spec:inputs), follows the status and log and cancels the pipeline on stop. Needs an API token with the api scope; without it only a trigger token run is possible.
settings.gen.type.jenkins_hint: Runs your job as is: LoadLens reads its parameters (strings, choices, flags, passwords, Active Choices), queues a build with the chosen values, follows it and stops it. For a multibranch job the branch is picked at launch.
settings.gen.type.kubernetes_hint: A Job per instance in a namespace. A service account token with rights to jobs, pods, pods/log and secrets of that namespace.
settings.gen.type.manual_hint: LoadLens starts nothing: the engineer starts the tool and marks the start and end of the run with buttons in LoadLens.
settings.gen.type.ssh_hint: LoadLens connects over SSH, starts the tool in the background and reads its log and exit code. GNU timeout and nohup are required.
settings.gen.wizard.changed: The connection data changed: check again.
settings.gen.wizard.check_optional: Without a check the generator is saved marked “not checked”.
settings.gen.wizard.ci_no_params: The pipeline declares no parameters: it runs with its default values.
settings.gen.wizard.ci_unchecked: The connection is not checked: the pipeline parameters are not read.
settings.gen.wizard.distrust_note: Without a pinned key LoadLens will not connect to the generator. Check the address and port: perhaps another server answered.
settings.gen.wizard.finish_unchecked: The connection is not checked: the generator is marked as not checked; you can check it in its card.
settings.gen.wizard.manual_no_check: A manual generator needs no check.
settings.gen.wizard.next_blocked: A passed connection check and a confirmed host key are needed
settings.gen.wizard.other_edits: Only the new generator is saved: other unsaved edits of the section stay in the form.
settings.gen.wizard.problems: The generator answers, but there are issues: {problems}. Until a check passes it is marked as not checked.
settings.gen.wizard.setup_note: The tool marks and the list below come from the check. Changed the directories? Check again.
settings.gen.wizard.setup_unchecked: The connection is not checked: directories and tools are not matched against the generator.
settings.gen.wizard.ssh_check_required: For SSH the check is required: it shows the host key you need to trust.
settings.gen.wizard.title: New load generator
settings.gen.wizard.title_note: Engineers see the name in the run form. LoadLens assigns the internal ID itself.
settings.kit.delete_confirm: “{id}” is removed once you save. Runs in progress on it go on, but LoadLens stops following them.
settings.llm.models_failed: Could not get the model list: {error}
settings.llm.models_unsupported: The provider does not list its models
settings.metrics.heading: Visualizations (metrics_config)
settings.metrics.help: Grafana panels and Loki logs for the Confluence template report: {sample_id}, {parent_id}, a {metrics} list with {grafana_url}, and {logs} with filters. Without a selected service you edit the configuration of the whole area (the {services} key).
settings.packs.bundle_help: Open the packs one by one: set the variables, check the queries and apply. Start with the load tool: load steps are found from it.
settings.packs.check_hint: The check runs the queries on the domain source for the window above.
settings.packs.check_ok: Source “{source}”: the required queries returned data.
settings.packs.dead_refs_note: References to queries that no longer exist are always replaced.
settings.packs.detect.alternative: The pack's metrics are in the source “{source}”: {found} of {total}.
settings.packs.detect.extra_sources: Also read, sources no domain is bound to: {list}.
settings.packs.detect.found_none: The source has none of the metrics
settings.packs.detect.hint: Reads the metric names of the domain sources and suggests matching packs and bundles.
settings.packs.detect.sorted: Packs are sorted by the metrics found in the sources.
settings.packs.domain_pick_hint: The queries of the pack go to the section of this domain, next to the metrics of the component itself.
settings.packs.installed_note: The pack is installed: the queries the domain has are ticked, the variables come from the installation.
settings.packs.instance_adds: Applying adds the installation “{name}” ({n} of {max}). Installations differ by the “{field}” field.
settings.packs.instance_updates: Applying updates the installation “{name}”. Another value of the “{field}” field adds a new one.
settings.packs.instances_full: The domain already has {max} installations: pick one, or type the title of one of them into the “{field}” field to update it.
settings.packs.mode_merge: Add and update the pack queries
settings.packs.mode_replace: Replace all queries of the domain
settings.packs.outdated_note: v{installed} is installed, v{latest} is available. The queries the domain already has and the new queries of this version ({count}) are ticked. The variables come from the installed pack; “Show changes” shows the update.
settings.packs.overwrite_sla: Replace references already set with the pack queries
settings.packs.plan.hint: Click “Show changes” to see which queries and SLA references will change.
settings.packs.remove_confirm: Domain queries will be deleted ({n}): {list}. Series with these names will no longer be collected. Continue?
settings.packs.scope_line: Applies to: {scope}. The domain queries and the SLA references of this scope will be updated.
settings.packs.source_hint: The queries of the pack read this source; the other rows of the domain keep theirs.
settings.packs.title: Query packs
settings.packs.unsaved_first: First save or discard the changes in the “Queries” and “SLA” sections: a pack is applied to the saved settings.
settings.packs.verified_title: All queries of the pack returned data on the docker/dev-stack bench with live exporters
settings.projects.help: A project is a project area with its own connections, SLA, queries, prompts and services. The “What is overridden” block shows where each setting comes from: “shared” means the global value; “copy of shared” means the project holds a copy that will not follow changes to the global value; “own” means the project value differs from the global one.
settings.prompts.discard_message: The current prompt is changed but not saved. Switch and lose the changes?
settings.prompts.heading: Prompts for the AI analysis
settings.prompts.help: Instructions for the model by domain. Placeholders such as {example} are filled in automatically and highlighted in the editor: do not remove them from the final prompt. Every save goes to the history, where an earlier version can be restored. Editing needs a selected area.
settings.prompts.history_empty: The history is empty: no earlier versions saved for this domain.
settings.prompts.history_loaded: The version is loaded into the editor: click “Save” to apply it
settings.prompts.missing_placeholders: The text lacks placeholders of the standard prompt: {list}; their data will not reach the model.
settings.prompts.override_lang.en: The override is in English and reports are in Russian; the answer will still be in Russian.
settings.prompts.override_lang.ru: The override is in Russian and reports are in English; the answer will still be in English.
settings.prompts.read_only: Read only: pick an area to edit
settings.prompts.reset_area: The area override is deleted; the standard text from the file comes back.
settings.prompts.reset_service: The service override is deleted; the area text will be used.
settings.prompts.service_load_failed: Could not load the service prompts: {error}
settings.queries.description_hint: Goes into the domain prompt next to the query name. Up to {max} characters.
settings.queries.description_hint_pack: The grey text is the description from the query pack: your text replaces it. Up to {max} characters.
settings.queries.description_placeholder: For example: rows in the outbox table; grows when the consumer falls behind
settings.queries.domain_title_hint: Empty means a title from the installed packs or the standard one. It is saved with every new report.
settings.queries.heading: Metric queries
settings.queries.help: Metric queries by domain. Click a query to edit it. The query name is used in the SLA and when comparing runs, so rename with care. Service settings override the area settings.
settings.queries.keys_shared: The label keys are shared by InfluxQL and Flux.
settings.queries.name_first: Set the name first: the role and the note belong to it.
settings.queries.role_hint: The role tells the AI analysis what the series means and its unit. A role with an SLA field fills an empty SLA reference with this query.
settings.queries.role_taken: Several queries of the domain have this role: an empty SLA reference takes the first of them, "{label}".
settings.queries.source_domain_note: The row reads the same source as the whole domain.
settings.queries.source_hint: A source of its own is needed when the metrics of the row are not where the other metrics of the domain are: node_exporter of a database host in a separate Prometheus, for example.
settings.queries.source_lang_mismatch: The source of the row does not run {lang}: pick another source or language.
settings.queries.source_pill_title: The row reads a source of its own, not the domain binding
settings.queries.summed_rps_confirm: The domain gets a row that adds up the total RPS of all tools (PromQL only), and it becomes the SLA throughput query: steps will be computed from the whole load of the combined test.
settings.queries.summed_rps_title: A row that adds up the total RPS of all tools of the domain; steps and the SLA will be computed from it
settings.queries.two_langs: The row has queries in {langs}; {lang} runs.
settings.services.add_known: Services from metrics_config without settings: {list}. You can enter another ID too: its visualization configuration is created from the template.
settings.services.add_message: Service ID in the area “{area}”: it is used in the report name and as the metrics_config key.
settings.services.delete_message: The service “{id}” is deleted together with its settings, metrics and reports. This cannot be undone.
settings.services.empty: This area has no services yet. Add the first one: its ID is used in the report name and as the metrics_config key.
settings.services.help: A service is the ID of a system under test inside an area; reports are created for it. Here you set its display name and choose the analysis domains; the service's queries, SLA, prompts and visualizations are set in their own sections by picking the service there.
settings.services.need_area: Services belong to areas: pick an area in the top bar or create a new one.
settings.services.no_metrics_config: not in metrics_config: panel snapshots are unavailable
settings.services.reset_done: The settings of the service “{id}” are reset
settings.services.reset_message: The custom settings of the service “{id}” (name, domains, prompts, queries, SLA, visualizations) are deleted. Reports and metrics stay.
settings.services.title_message: How to show the service in the interface (optional).
settings.sla.dead_ref: The query “{name}” is gone: the criterion gets no data. Pick another query.
settings.sla.dead_ref_auto: The query “{name}” is gone. The report takes “{auto}” by its role; pick a query and save.
settings.sla.field.latency_unit: Response time units in the P95, P99 and mean queries
settings.sla.field.load_model_hint: Open: concurrency = RPS × mean response time. Closed: concurrency = number of VUs.
settings.sla.field.service_cpu_query_hin: CPU share of one instance from 0 to 1 by (service, instance), for example process_cpu_usage by (application, instance). It tells how many pods the target needs.
settings.sla.field.step_detection_enable: Use the step detector (step and stress tests)
settings.sla.field.target_margin_pct_hin: Step and stress tests: the latency and error thresholds must also hold at the target RPS plus the margin, otherwise the verdict is "Risks found"; CPU and memory are then checked on that step. Empty: no margin.
settings.sla.field.target_rps_allow_peak: No stable step: use the peak RPS
settings.sla.field.target_rps_desc: The main criterion. Step and stress tests: reached on a step where the latency and error thresholds hold; the steps above the target are headroom and do not affect the verdict. Soak: held for the whole test; spike: the spike level.
settings.sla.forecast_help: Queries and the load model for the “Forecasting” page.
settings.sla.help: Tick the criteria to check and set their thresholds. The main criterion is the target RPS: if it is reached on a stable step, the test passes, and breaches of the other thresholds give the verdict “{risk}”. Unticked criteria are not checked.
settings.sla.peak_help: The RPS query is chosen in the “Target RPS” row. Here you set how stable load steps are found.
settings.sla.rename_confirm: “{from}” is used in the SLA ({usage}). Update the references to “{to}”?
settings.sla.rename_done: The SLA references are updated in the form. Save the SLA section.
settings.sla.shared_desc: Error rate and latency: the 95th percentile over stable_max (the last step where they hold), before RPS drops; the tail after the plateau is left out. CPU and memory: on the target step (the first step at the target RPS) when a target is set. For soak it is the hold window, for spike the worst spike. Thresholds are in the units of the query.
settings.source.delete_confirm: The source “{id}” leaves the catalog once you save. If domains refer to it, saving fails and shows where it is used.
settings.source.empty: No sources yet. Add a connection to Grafana, Prometheus or InfluxDB.
settings.source.id_hint: Domains refer to the source by its ID; it cannot be changed after saving.
settings.source.type.grafana_proxy_hint: Queries go through Grafana: PromQL, InfluxQL and Flux over its data sources. Each domain picks its data source.
settings.source.type.influxdb_hint: Flux queries straight to InfluxDB 2.x. The bucket is set per domain.
settings.source.type.prometheus_hint: PromQL queries straight to Prometheus or a compatible API.
settings.source.type_unsupported: This source type is not supported: delete it and add it again.
settings.title: Settings
settings.tool.empty: No tools: add a command template.
settings.tool.hint: The command is built from the template: it is split into words first, then the values are put into each word, so a value never becomes several arguments.
settings.users.help: {viewer} sees reports, the archive, comparisons and forecasts. {engineer} can also run analyses, publish to Confluence, write notes and give ratings. {admin} can also change settings and connections, delete data and manage users. A lockout after failed sign-ins is lifted with the “Unlock” button.
settings.wizard.done_help: The connections are checked. You can load a demo run to see a report without real data, or create your first report right away.
settings.wizard.hint.check_or_skip: Test the connection to go on, or skip the step.
settings.wizard.hint.checked: The connection is checked: you can go on.
settings.wizard.hint.language: Choose the language of reports and prompts and click “Next”. The interface language is in the View menu of the top bar.
settings.wizard.hint.queries_needed: Click “Add from a pack” and pick a bundle for your stack: at least the load tool queries are needed. You can skip the step.
settings.wizard.hint.queries_ok: The load tool queries are set: you can go on.
settings.wizard.hint.sla: Set the thresholds (you can do it later) and click “Next”.
settings.wizard.hint_initial: Test the connection to go on.
